roleNote: An example of what you can build from kit components. Start from it, change it, or ignore it; layout is your choice. Follow `must` (kit look and accessibility); `defaults` are this example's suggestions, change any of them.
copyNote: Not exported from agentic-ds-kit. add copies the source into your app (components/patterns/app-shell/) with this contract beside it. You own the copy: replace the demo data, rearrange or drop sections, and keep the `must` lines.
intent: One layout option, as a copy-in example: AppHeader over SideNav + content when wide (>= --grid-breakpoint-md, 64rem; layout-shell / layout-app, radius none, no gap); narrow, the SideNav moves into a left Drawer opened by a Menu Button at the start of AppHeader. Top bar only, side nav only, or neither are equally fine: compose AppHeader, SideNav, and Drawer yourself.

header.note: AppHeader props except radius (always none); on narrow screens the shell puts the Menu Button in the logo slot, so the mark or logo shows only when wide. Known gap: a start slot replaces the whole brand cell, logo included, so a props header with start loses the injected Menu Button; put AppShellPattern.MenuButton inside your start (or build the header from blocks). Or a header node built from AppHeader.Root and its blocks: then the shell injects nothing and the header must place AppShellPattern.MenuButton (usually as the AppHeader.Brand logo).

nav.note: SideNav props except showHeader, radius, and side: title, mark, groups or items, footer, open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange for the wide rail. The Drawer shows the same data, always expanded, titled nav.title. Or a nav node you built (a SideNav preset, or SideNavRoot with SideNavNav / SideNavSection / SideNavItem and the other blocks): the shell renders it in the rail when wide and inside the Drawer when narrow; it reads useAppShell().navPlacement to adapt (showHeader false; radius none in the rail, md and always expanded in the Drawer). Or a function (placement: rail | drawer) => node, so a nav that takes a placement prop (ShellNav from add side-nav) needs no hook.

navLabel.note: Drawer title on narrow screens. Default nav.title, or Navigation for a built nav.

children.note: Page content: a layout-canvas or layout-workspace, or another pattern. Pages own their one primary Button.

className.note: Extra class on the layout-shell root, e.g. to give it the viewport height.

customChrome.note: header and nav accept nodes built from kit blocks. The shell keeps the layout (layout-shell over layout-app, no gap), the breakpoint, and the Drawer.

exports.AppShellPattern.MenuButton: Also AppShellMenuButton (use the named export from Server Components). Exported from your app-shell copy. Tertiary sm Menu Button that opens the nav Drawer when narrow; renders its children when wide (e.g. <AppHeader.Mark>A</AppHeader.Mark>). Focus returns to it when the Drawer closes. ariaLabel default Open navigation.
exports.useAppShell(): Exported from your app-shell copy. Inside the shell: { narrow, navOpen, openNav, closeNav, navPlacement: rail | drawer | null }. Null outside AppShellPattern. Client components only.

rules: A built header must contain AppShellPattern.MenuButton; without it the shell warns and narrow screens cannot reach the nav
Put the Menu Button in AppHeader.Brand's logo so it sits on the rail axis, as the preset does
A built nav is one landmark (SideNav preset or SideNavRoot + blocks); the same node moves between rail and Drawer, it is never rendered twice
Build the nav from the named block exports (SideNavRoot, SideNavSlot, SideNavNav, SideNavSection, SideNavItem, SideNavFooter): they work from Server Components, where SideNav.Root dot access does not
In the shell, drop SideNavHeader and SideNavToggle (AppHeader has the brand and the Menu Button); in the Drawer force the nav open (open, or inDrawer || open) so it is never a closed rail
A props header that sets start loses the injected Menu Button: place AppShellPattern.MenuButton inside your start
In the Drawer, radius md; leaf picks close the Drawer, disclosures (aria-expanded) do not

customChrome.copyIn: npx agentic-ds-kit add app-header and add side-nav copy ShellHeader (AppHeader blocks) and ShellNav (SideNavRoot / Nav / Section / Item / Footer blocks). Both import only kit components and work without app-shell. To host them here (in a client component): header={<ShellHeader menuButton={AppShellMenuButton} />} nav={(placement) => <ShellNav placement={placement} />}.

responsive.breakpoint: --grid-breakpoint-md (64rem). matchMedia reads the token at runtime; the CSS module repeats 64rem only for the first paint before hydration.
narrow: No SideNav in the layout; content takes the full width
Menu Button (tertiary sm, lucide Menu, ariaLabel "Open navigation") sits in AppHeader's start column
Left Drawer size sm holds SideNav showHeader false, always expanded
Picking a leaf, Escape, or a scrim click closes the Drawer; focus returns to the Menu Button
AppHeader search stays an Input; below 38rem AppHeader already stacks it under the brand row
Widening past the breakpoint closes the Drawer and brings SideNav back without a reload

requirements: Menu Button is a kit Button with ariaLabel "Open navigation"
The Drawer is the kit dialog: aria-modal, focus trapped, Escape and scrim close, focus restored to the trigger
Parent nav items (disclosures) do not close the Drawer; leaves do
Active leaf keeps aria-current=page in both SideNav and the Drawer
With a built header, AppShellPattern.MenuButton is the only Drawer trigger; it carries the same label and focus return as the injected one

must: Semantic tokens only (agentic-ds-kit/tokens.css); no raw hex, no primitive --color-* ramps
At most one variant="primary" Button per view; the shell has none, pages own theirs
Do not restyle kit components; change them through their props, slots, and tokens

Render inside a main landmark (wrap the pattern, or your page content, in <main>); header and nav chrome, if any, use AppHeader / SideNav (or other header / nav landmarks) and nav stays reachable on small screens
Overlays are kit Drawer or Modal (focus trap, Escape, scrim, focus return built in); no local scrim, sheet, or fixed overlay, and SideNav itself is never an overlay
Breakpoints follow --grid-breakpoint-md: matchMedia reads the token; media queries cannot read var(), so CSS repeats 64rem with a comment naming the token
A custom header places AppShellMenuButton (accessible name and focus return built in); without it narrow screens cannot reach the nav
defaults: Narrow screens: the nav moves into a left kit Drawer behind a Menu Button; another pattern is fine as long as the nav stays reachable
The Menu Button sits at the start of AppHeader, in the brand cell on the rail axis
Below the breakpoint there is no fixed SideNav or collapsed rail; the Drawer holds the nav
Chrome is layout-shell (AppHeader, radius none) over layout-app (SideNav, radius none, no header), no gap
One layout option among many: top bar only, side nav only, both, or neither are all fine
